ledger.claim: The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace. The trace runs 28.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booking optimal of 22.4 km: an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed - the excess is greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20% of the optimal route - so the establishment test is met on both limbs. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (28.18 km), not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 28.2, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The excess may be proved on the trace alone. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 229 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and a 10 second sample interval well below the 30 second sustained-interval limb. No independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is therefore required, and the strongest evidence in the bundle is also its cleanest (weight_multiplier 1.0).

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00115, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-08T21:10:00 matches the trip_record started_at of 2026-08-08T21:10:00, so the artifacts describe the same trip. POL-RD-08(b) is satisfied by the 25.80% excess measured on an unimpaired trace. The burden has shifted to the driver, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was heavy, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it.

No corroboration beyond the trace attaches to this claim. POL-RD-08's additional corroboration requirement bites only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. The rider's counters are 0 and 0, so the below-30% excess of 25.80% needs nothing further and the factor cannot be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The measure of the rider's loss is fixed by the fare model. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 non-null, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time lines were settled at booking and the rider's entitlement is the POL-RD-11(a) correction - the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus only those pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That is the clause under which the rider is paid, and it does not depend on the size of the detour.

The arithmetic on POL-RD-11(a): charged_total is 39.00 and quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50, an overage of 4.50, all of it on the tolls_erp line. Of the two ERP lines only the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge of 2.50 is properly chargeable, because it lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 44.50 m of that gantry. The refund is therefore 39.00 - 34.50 - 2.50 = SGD 2.00, payable to the rider.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a phantom charge and is refundable in full. It is not on the optimal route, and the trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419.29 m - more than twenty times the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) applies - so the vehicle never crossed it and no fix takes it within the billed corridor. Under POL-RD-09(4) this is a billing-integrity failure, refunded as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list.

The SGD 2.00 must not be counted twice in the rider's favour. POL-RD-09(1) and the POL-RD-11 note both bar adding the POL-RD-11(b) pass-through correction on top of the POL-RD-11(a) figure, because the phantom line is already excluded from the properly chargeable total; counting it again would refund it twice. The rider's total recovery is SGD 2.00, and I put that figure forward as the correct one rather than inflate it.

The driver's explanation that 'CTE northbound was heavy' carries no weight. The bundle's only traffic advisory is EV-ADVIS-00115-01, which is MISSING - issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING severity, weight_multiplier 0.0 - and I cite the absence itself and disclose that the artifact carries no weight. No advisory covers the CTE, the KPE or the TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window. Under POL-RD-13 POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record, and under POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion does not discharge the driver's burden. The deviation stands at the measured 5.78 km and no closure-adjusted or amended optimal may be substituted for the booked one.

The absent advisory is not an escalation trigger. The artifact EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT), and I disclose that. POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion which names no evidence ID cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): the driver cited no advisory identifier, so the gap in the bundle is not a contradiction in it. The same limb makes clear that this does not narrow POL-RD-10(5) where a party does cite the missing identifier, which no party here did. The case is ruleable on the present record, and the disputed amount should be returned rather than held.

The chat log does not exonerate the driver. The only rider message is 'ok' at 21:14:50, acknowledging the driver's own 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE'. It comes from the rider but it instructs nothing and identifies no place or road specifically enough to act on, and both messages carry waypoint_hint null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction meeting all three of its limbs, so the clause is unavailable to the driver, no distance is excluded from the excess and no exclusion is earned by the driver having told the rider what he was doing.

The phantom AYE line does not force escalation under POL-RD-10(8). That limb expressly excepts a charge line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and the AYE line is the only unmatched line in this breakdown; the KPE line has its counterpart in the trace and the trip record. The case can be decided now by a monetary ruling, with the SGD 2.00 returned to the rider, rather than escalated with the amount frozen.

This trip was sold to the rider at a fixed UPFRONT_QUOTE of SGD 34.50, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run on this fare: no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the measured excess. The rider's demand to be refunded for 'the extra distance' therefore fails as a matter of the governing clause, and the driver discharges the burden POL-RD-08 places on him by pointing to the fare_model field carried on the fare breakdown.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's recovery is limited to the amount by which the SGD 39.00 charged total exceeds the SGD 34.50 quoted fare plus only the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and the record's own money block computes that figure as SGD 2.00. That single line is the whole of the driver's monetary exposure on this trip; the remaining SGD 4.00 of the contested SGD 6.00 is unsupported.

The SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 and must not be refunded: it lies on the optimal route (on_optimal_route true) and the trace actually crossed it, the nearest fix being 44.5 m from the gantry, well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 applies. It is neither an off-route line nor a phantom line.

The driver does not contest the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line, and no honest argument is available to him on it: the trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419 m and the line carries on_optimal_route false and crossed false, and the driver's own statement is that he never went there. Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction. It is a defect on the platform's payments ledger, not a route the driver drove, and it caps the rider's success at SGD 2.00.

Even taking the rider's own figures, the excess is 5.78 km and 25.8% of the 22.4 km optimal route. That passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gate but falls short of both materiality limbs (greater than 50% of optimal, or greater than 8.0 km absolute), so the deviation on this trip is not MATERIAL and POL-RD-06's driver-profile check, its FULL_REFUND uplift and its conduct referral are not engaged.

In any event the citable POL-RD-06 counters exculpate the driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the pattern threshold of 3, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 523 is 0.0019, far below the 0.05 ratio test. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, and no uplift or referral follows even if the profile is consulted.

The only traffic_advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver's explanation that the CTE was heavy therefore cannot be tested against POL-RD-03, which is unavailable, and under POL-RD-13 that assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. Because the driver cites no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than the POL-RD-10(5) escalation that might otherwise be argued, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

Nothing in POL-RD-10 sends this case to a human reviewer. The trip identifiers and pickup timestamps match across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), carrying 229 fixes at a constant 10 s interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0; and the only unmatched charge line is the AYE gantry refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from its trigger. The dispute is therefore resolvable on the money, at the SGD 2.00 ceiling.

The chat log shows the driver told the rider of the diversion before it was driven ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE') and the rider acknowledged it with 'ok'; the rider was on notice of the KPE-then-TPE route from 21:14:50 and never objected, so there is no question of concealment. POL-RD-04's exoneration nonetheless cannot be run on this record, because the rider's message identifies no place or road and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the driver does not rely on it and this dispute is decided on the fare model and the ERP lines.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. The trip was booked on an UPFRONT_QUOTE and the card was charged SGD 39.00 against a quoted fare of SGD 34.50 — an overage of SGD 4.50, all of it on the tolls/ERP line. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so no distance-or-time refund is available on this fare: the rider's request to be refunded for 'the extra distance' is refused as a matter of the governing clause. The trace did run 28.18 km against an optimal 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km / 25.8%, which is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 but is not a MATERIAL deviation (both materiality limbs — over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km — fail), so no POL-RD-06 pattern test, uplift or conduct referral arises on this trip. What the rider does recover is the overage the platform should not have charged. Of the two ERP lines, the SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge is properly chargeable: it lies on the optimal route and the trace passes 44.5 m from that gantry, inside the 250 m match radius. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is a phantom charge — it is not on the optimal route and the trace's closest approach is 5,419 m — so under POL-RD-09(4) it is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction. The refund is 39.00 − 34.50 − 2.50 = SGD 2.00, and it is not doubled: POL-RD-09(1) and the fare note bar adding the POL-RD-11(b) pass-through correction on top of the POL-RD-11(a) figure, because the phantom line is already excluded from the properly chargeable total. The driver's explanation that 'CTE northbound was heavy' cannot be tested: the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the trip window, so under POL-RD-13 POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 — it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. It is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because no advisory identifier was relied on by the asserting party; the missing artifact is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. The chat log shows the driver announced the KPE-then-TPE diversion and the rider replied 'ok'; that is not a rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04 (the rider named no place or road and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null), so no distance is excluded and the clause is simply unavailable to either side. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (229 fixes, 100% coverage, 10 s interval, max_gap_sec 0.0), so no independent-corroboration issue arises and the deviation stands at the measured 5.78 km. The ruling rests on EV-FARE-00115 and EV-GPS-00115, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the platform floor. The SGD 2.00 monetary effect is within the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and executes automatically under POL-GEN-05; the billing-integrity referral does not delay or displace the money.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: review the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) ERP line charged on TRP-00115 — a phantom gantry the GPS trace never came within 5,419 m of and which is not on the optimal route; refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction.
